core_condition: at least one measured effect recorded in observed_effects from Ventora telemetry or public corpora

evidence.rationale: The reciprocity norm (Gouldner 1960) is a foundational and broadly accepted social rule, and reciprocity underlies well-studied compliance techniques (door-in-the-face; gift-exchange field experiments). Scored 2 rather than 3 because much of the applied persuasion literature is demonstration-based, effect sizes in commercial digital contexts are less rigorously established, and door-in-the-face/compliance findings have some replication variability.

product_applicability.rationale: Directly implementable via value-first lead magnets, free tools, and unexpected upgrades. Ventora's own free Idea Check funnel is a live reciprocity mechanism. High applicability at top and middle of funnel.

measurability.rationale: Maps to signup_rate, cvr, conversion_after_gift, retention_lift — Amplitude-reachable and A/B-testable.

orthogonality.rationale: Distinct from EN-03 (obligation-to-return vs valuation-of-owned) and SP-08 (exchange obligation vs others-as-evidence). Clear boundaries.

safety.rationale: Value-first giving is among the most benign mechanisms — it front-loads genuine user benefit. Risks are hollow gifts, coercive obligation framing, and unsolicited-gift-as-leverage (forced trials that auto-bill), all blocked by hard rules and covered by negative-option/inertia-selling regulation. Clear boundary, hence 3.

dissent: Two cautions. (1) The compliance-technique literature (door-in-the-face, that's-not-all) that popularized reciprocity in persuasion has uneven replication and effect sizes smaller than early demonstrations; we lean on the robust norm itself (Gouldner, gift-exchange field evidence) rather than specific compliance tricks. (2) Reciprocity weakens or reverses when perceived as manipulation — a transparent quid-pro-quo ('we gave you X, now buy Y') triggers reactance. We therefore claim genuine, standalone-useful value given first, and block manufactured obligation.

evidence_sources.ref: Gouldner (1960). The Norm of Reciprocity: A Preliminary Statement. American Sociological Review 25(2).
Cialdini et al. (1975). Reciprocal concessions procedure (door-in-the-face). JPSP 31(2).
